about.text: Stracciatella is a fresh cheese originating from Apulia, Italy, made by shredding stretched curd and, traditionally, mixing it with cream. It may be produced from either cow's milk or Italian buffalo milk, depending on the mozzarella used.

how.text: Part of the stretched curd is torn by hand into strips and soaked in cream. This spongy, half-liquid filling (stracciatella) spills out when a burrata is cut.
